drawings.description: figures : (C$_1$), au crayon et à l'encre, l'icosaèdre vu le long d'un axe passant par les milieux de deux arêtes opposées, sommets $u, v$, $u', v'$, $s, t$, $\Pi_{s,u}$, $\Pi_{t,v}$, … ; « ou » (C$_2$), la même vue en projection, sommets extérieurs $s'$, $u'$, $v'$, $t'$, points $\Pi_{t,u} = \Pi_{s',v'}$ (?), $\Pi_{t,v} = \Pi_{s',u'}$, $\Pi_{s,u} = \Pi_{t',v'}$, $\Pi_{s,v} = \Pi_{t',u'}$ ; (C$_3$), un schéma analogue plus petit, flèches vers $t'$ et $s'$
drawings.kind: icosahedron seen along an axis (three views)
drawings.notes: Redrawn from a fresh crop of p. 8 (issue 128), 1 unit = 1.8 mm. (C1) the icosahedron seen along the axis through the midpoints of two opposite edges, all 30 edges as on the page: the front edge t-s vertical, u and v at the sides, the four Pi vertices at the corners, the 17 visible edges solid; the hidden ones dashed: the two back side vertices (inside u and v) joined to the Pi corners and to the two ends of the back edge, which he draws a little above t and s (the back edge itself, on the line t-s, is not drawn separately). (C2) the same in projection: the back vertices s' (top), t' (bottom), v' (left), u' (right) outside, the four outer edges between them being the arcs of the circle (drawn as one closed curve; on the page it is in four heavy arcs with small gaps); the Pi points on the lines from the outer vertices, u and v on the sides of the Pi square, t and s computed as the crossings of the lines Pi-t-v and Pi-t-u (resp. Pi-s-v, Pi-s-u), which he draws straight; the vertical arrows to t' (up) and s' (down); the Pi labels with their equalities as on the page. (C3) the same scheme, smaller, with straight outer edges and arrows to t' and s'. Labels (C1), (C2), (C3) and "ou" placed as on the page. Pencil doublings drawn once. Left out: a small c-shaped mark at the centre of C2 and two small marks inside C2 just below s' and above t' (read as letters, not legible). Still differs: the side labels of the back vertices are written like u' on both sides in C1 and on the left in C2; the redraw writes v' on the left, as the transcription and the equalities Pi_{t,u} = Pi_{s',v'} require. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: en marge gauche, un croquis : l'arête $a = \{s, t\}$, les sommets $u$, $v$, et les quatre sommets $\Pi_{s,u}$, $\Pi_{s,v}$, $\Pi_{t,u}$, $\Pi_{t,v}$ aux coins d'un rectangle. Les indices des $\Pi$ sont serrés et parfois surchargés ; ils sont donnés tels que l'argument les appelle (cf.\ page~8, où apparaît la même notation $\Pi_{s,u}$)
drawings.kind: neighbourhood of an edge of the icosahedron (planar)
drawings.notes: The edge a = {s, t} (vertical, in the middle), the vertices u, v on either side, and the four vertices Pi_{s,u}, Pi_{s,v}, Pi_{t,u}, Pi_{t,v} at the corners of a rectangle; s and t are joined to u, v and to their two Pi corners. Labels after the transcription (the indices of the Pi are cramped).

drawings.description: à gauche, un dessin de l'icosaèdre en perspective, arêtes cachées en pointillé ; sommets marqués $u_1$, $w_1'$, $u'$, $v_1'$, $w$, $v$, $v_1$, $w_1$, $u = s$, $u_1'$, $w'$, $v'$ ; un triangle fondamental hachuré, de sommet $s$, porte sur ses côtés les marques $\sigma_0$, $\sigma_1$, $\sigma_2$
drawings.notes: Icosahedron with its hidden edges dashed; vertices u_1, w_1', v_1', v_1, w_1, u_1' on the outline, w, v, u = s in front, u', v', w' behind. Encoded as polyhedron/1 with the labels of the page (u=s for the front vertex); the 12 dashed edges are read from scattered dashes and checked against the icosahedron (every vertex of degree 5). The hatched fundamental triangle with apex s carries sigma_0, sigma_1, sigma_2 on its sides.

drawings.description: dans la marge gauche, trois croquis : un pentagone de sommets $t = \tau$, $u$, $v$, $\tilde{u}$, $\tilde{v}$, de centre $s$, marqué $(\pi)$ ; sous lui, une colonne de paires fléchées en cycle, $\{s, u\} \to \{s, v\} \to \{s, \tilde{u}\} \sim \{t, v\}$, $\{s, \tilde{v}\} \sim \{t, u\}$, au-dessus d'un premier essai biffé ; plus bas, un fragment d'icosaèdre de sommets $u$, $v$, $w$, $u_1$, $v_1$, $w_1$, l'arête $\{u, v\}$ épaissie, et le cycle $\{u, w_1\} \to \{w_1, v\} \to \{v, w\} \to \{w, u\}$
drawings.kind: pentagon, cycle of pairs, fragment of icosahedron (margin)
drawings.notes: Three margin sketches. (1) Pentagon t = tau, v, v~, u~, u with centre s, marked (pi), the side and spoke at t thickened. (2) The column of arrowed pairs {s,u} -> {s,v} -> {s,u~} ~ {t,v}, {s,v~} ~ {t,u}, with the arrow closing the cycle on the left; above it the first attempt, hatched and struck, is only indicated by grey strokes. (3) Fragment of the icosahedron with u, v, w, u_1, v_1, w_1, the edge {u, v} thickened, and the cycle {u,w_1} -> {w_1,v} -> {v,w} -> {w,u} with its loop arrow. The exact edges of (3) are a reading. Issue 128 pass: The first attempt above the column of pairs, hatched and struck on the page, is no longer drawn (it was drawn grey). Line ends that nearly met were merged into one computed vertex, and the labels set at \small. Still differs, not re-read in this pass: the positions and edges as noted above. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: sous un croquis de pentagone à diagonales, de sommets $u$, $v$, marqué $a$, $s$, $f$
drawings.notes: Pentagon (five vertices computed once, every side drawn between them); the diagonal from the top vertex to the lower right heavy; the diagonal from the bottom vertex to the upper right, heavy in its lower half; and a third stroke from the left vertex to the crossing point of the two diagonals (computed). Letters as on the page: a (upper inner region), a second inner letter like s (a reading), f (lower inner region), s outside at the lower right, u under the bottom vertex. Still differs: the vertex v of the transcription is not identified on the facsimile and is left unlabelled; the marginal "NB a ~ {u, v}" is text and left out. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again.
